frequency_question: How frequently do states under high-intensity existential conflict successfully establish domestic production of complex foreign military systems within a multi-year window when prioritized by leadership?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states fighting a major conventional war that initiated domestic assembly/manufacturing lines for advanced foreign-supplied guided weapons or heavy munitions. Excludes simple small-arms or low-tech ammunition production.

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production of Stugna-P and Neptune missiles (wartime scaling)
Ukraine domestic production of various FPV and long-range strike drones
UK wartime dispersal and shadow factory production of complex aircraft/munitions
Russian domestic assembly/adaptation of Iranian-designed Shahed loitering munitions
Ukraine joint-venture heavy armor production setup (e.g., Rheinmetall agreements)

coverage_note: 5 major instances enumerated covering modern and historical urgent localized defense manufacturing under duress.
known_gaps: Extremely complex cruise missile tech transfer involves proprietary intellectual property and specialized chemical inputs that have fewer direct historical analogues than drones or artillery.
skeleton: Wartime urgent defense industrial mobilization cases for complex systems
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 comparable major historical/contemporary urgent defense localization efforts
validity_reason: Base rate tied to contemporary defense-industrial mobilization practices and technological diffusion speeds, valid for several years.
